sources.title: Smith GM, Ruebens K, Zavala EI, et al. (2024). The ecology, subsistence and diet of ~45,000-year-old Homo sapiens at Ilsenhöhle in Ranis, Germany. Nature Ecology & Evolution 8:564–577.
sources.version: Nature Ecology & Evolution 8(3):564–577; version of record published 2024-01-31
sources.locator: Abstract; Main—stable-isotope analysis and Ilsenhöhle stratigraphy; Rights and permissions.
sources.scope: Primary zooarchaeology and stable-isotope study at one cave in Ranis, Germany. The human diet inference is limited to 10 sampled human remains and their archaeological context.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, as recorded in the repository dossier source audit.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: PMC-hosted full text, Open Access notice; CC BY 4.0
sources.attribution: Smith GM, Ruebens K, Zavala EI, et al. (2024). The ecology, subsistence and diet of ~45,000-year-old Homo sapiens at Ilsenhöhle in Ranis, Germany. Nature Ecology & Evolution 8:564–577. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-023-02303-6. Claims are paraphrased; no figures or tables are reproduced.

claims.text: The study assigns fossil remains TPL 6 and TPL 7 to Homo sapiens; the cave sequence model places TPL 6 at 70 ± 3 ka and extends the record with TPL 7 to 77 ± 9 ka. These are depositional-context estimates, not direct dates on the human fragments.
claims.scope: One cave sequence. TPL 7 may predate the modeled age because the deepest sediment sample was collected higher in the section.

claims.text: TPL 6 is a partial left frontal bone with a modest superciliary arch and no supraorbital torus; geometric-morphometric projections place the reconstruction among relatively gracile frontal forms. Taphonomic alteration of TPL 7 prevents accurate osteometric analysis.
claims.scope: Descriptions concern two specimens from one locality and do not estimate species-wide anatomical variation.

claims.text: Stable-isotope analysis of collagen from 10 human remains, interpreted with 52 animal remains, supports a dietary signal dominated by large terrestrial mammals for the sampled people at Ilsenhöhle in Ranis.
claims.scope: One cave and its archaeological context; isotope evidence does not prove every indicated animal taxon was consumed there or establish a general human diet.

gaps: This is a selected research guide, not a systematic species-wide dossier or a global fossil-range review.
The evidence does not assess current distribution, population trend, life history, or formal conservation status.
